findings.why: From here Earth's orbit is tilted 53.130° from edge-on; it would need to be within 0.269° to cross the star's face, so it never transits.

Earth swings the star towards and away from here by 0.054 m/s every 365.3 days; 877 measurements at 1.00 m/s (with the star's own 1.0 m/s jitter) give 0.8σ. Only the minimum mass is measured: the tilt is unknown.
Earth drags the star round a circle 0.6 µas across on the sky every 1.0 years; 877 positions at 20 µas give 0.3σ. This gives the true mass and the tilt.
From here Jupiter's orbit is tilted 54.411° from edge-on; it would need to be within 0.056° to cross the star's face, so it never transits.

Jupiter swings the star towards and away from here by 7.260 m/s every 4332.3 days; 877 measurements at 1.00 m/s (with the star's own 1.0 m/s jitter) give 107.5σ. Only the minimum mass is measured: the tilt is unknown.
Jupiter drags the star round a circle 993.3 µas across on the sky every 11.9 years; 877 positions at 20 µas give 519.9σ. This gives the true mass and the tilt.
